UK COMMERCIAL GUIDES

A remarkable presence.
A substantial care plan.

Research macaws, cockatoos and other larger parrots around usable space, noise and long-term care.

Think in practical terms

A large parrot can be visually striking, but choosing one should begin with the household environment. Consider room for exercise, suitable accommodation, durable equipment and a sustainable daily routine. Powerful beaks and loud vocalisation deserve attention before a buying enquiry.

Explore the macaw profile and cockatoo profile as different groups rather than one interchangeable category.

Plan for long-term care

Some larger parrots can remain companions for decades. Think about future household changes and who could provide care if you were unavailable. Review ongoing food, equipment and veterinary costs as well as the price of the bird.

The parrot price planning page helps separate the purchase from lifetime costs. Actual prices must be confirmed for the individual.

Discuss the individual and the home

Ask about background, current diet, handling preferences and response to unfamiliar people. Describe the space available and the experience of everyone involved in care. Size alone does not tell you the bird’s temperament.

Use the macaw buying enquiry page or cockatoo buying enquiry page for the questions to resolve before committing.
